This indicator measures changes in policy and strategic frameworks directly resulting from project activities aimed at promoting women’s voice, agency, leadership, and representative participation in decision-making across public, private, and civic spheres. 1 Governmental policies was improved to promote women’s voice, agency, leadership, and representative participation in decision-making processes in public, private and civic sphere durong the reporting period.
None was planned

Important government policies meant to increase women's involvement in decision-making have been adopted, thanks in part to the advocacy efforts of WROs and AS in Somalia. Their efforts produced a women's quota for the parliament of Somalia, adopted in April 2021. Still, just 24% of the federal parliamentary seats are occupied by women at present. This has led to demands for the quota to be fully applied. Notwithstanding opposition, ongoing campaigning by women's coalitions, CSOs, and political influencers effectively passed the one-man, one-vote election modality in parliament, which is expected to provide chances for political engagement for women and young people.

Advocacy and Lobbying campaign for Somalia women’s participation in the 2022 political process and to increase representation seats at all level of government bodies and leadership positions up to 30% (i.e. through National electoral law). We will also create strategic guidance frameworks to address the processes of inclusive politics and democratization in state-level elections and advocate for the role of women in the process through Civic engagement awareness, media campaigns and involvement in state-level electoral law process
In 2021, the focus will be on mapping and identifying WRAs and Os to participate in the project, establishing coalitions, and engaging in capacity-building activities for the WRAs and Os.
In Somalia, they proposed the Women’s Economic Empowerment Policy and a Gender Media Policy to expand women’s participation in public and civic life.

Advocate and lobby for the passing of the 2018 SOB or amendments to the bill that would protect women and girls against SGBV.

Although not completely achieved, legislative advocacy by WRA/Os on the SOB has greatly advanced women's rights. Accomplished by social media campaigns, media-oriented mass rallies, and discussions with parliamentary committees, Puntland's ratification of the zero-tolerance FGM bill stands apart. Still, difficulties exist since the Rape and Immoral Bill—formerly SOB—was first rejected because of misunderstandings and opposition. Notwithstanding political unrest and competing interests, ongoing advocacy by WROs/As, civil society organizations, and important ministries has helped the bill pass several review phases; it is now pending final review in parliament.
Advocate for the adoption of the 2018 SOB or amendment to better protect the rights of women and girls.
In 2021, the focus will be on mapping and identifying WRAs and Os to participate in the project, establishing coalitions, and engaging in capacity-building activities for the WRAs and Os.region.
Continue with policy and legal reforms

In 2024, the WRA/Os reported influencing 5 laws, policies, and strategies to strengthen women’s agency and leadership, including the Sexual Offences Bill (SOB), zero-tolerance legislation for FGM in Garowe, and laws promoting women’s political participation through affirmative action. They also proposed the Women’s Economic Empowerment Policy and a Gender Media Policy, demonstrating how WROs are driving reforms that increase women’s participation in public and civic life.
Continue to lobby and advocate for the revision of certain chapters of the newly introduced Rape and Immorality Bill, which is still in Parliament.

NAGAAD and its partners will target individuals in the three specified regions; this will includewomen in their broader membership base, young women, local women civil society organisations,and women civic and parliamentary candidates to encompass both political, economic and culturalrights. Subsequently, the advocacy and lobbying arm of this project will heavily focus on influencersand policymakers at the national level. We will work towards reducing the barriers to women's participation in decision making processes by building their capacity on the available legal frameworks that supports them. NAGAAD and its partners will target individuals in the three specified regions; this will includewomen in their broader membership base, young women, local women civil society organisations,and women civic and parliamentary candidates to encompass both political, economic and culturalrights. Subsequently, the advocacy and lobbying arm of this project will heavily focus on influencersand policymakers at the national level. This includes the line ministries, media houses, ParliamentarySocial Committee, members of Parliament in the House of Representatives and House of Elders(Guurti), political parties and their related officials, clan/religious leaders and the ElectoralCommission.
